citations.title: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
Empirical Explorations with the Logic Theory Machine: A Case Study in Heuristics

claims.statement: Cybernetics organized feedback, control, and communication across animal and machine systems without being identical to contemporary machine learning.
claims.scope: Wiener's postwar research program and terminology

claims.statement: Idealized neural units were formally related to logical operations in an abstract network model.
claims.scope: the source's formal model, not biological fidelity or modern training

claims.statement: Turing proposed the imitation game as an operational reframing and discussed objections and learning machines.
claims.scope: the 1950 paper rather than every later conversational benchmark

claims.statement: The Logic Theory Machine used symbolic representations and heuristic search to find proofs in a bounded formal domain.
claims.scope: the documented program and selected proof tasks

uncertainty: Later field labels are retrospective and may hide differences in the sources' own categories.
Four sources cannot exhaust the institutions, countries, methods, or precursors relevant to early machine intelligence.
Conceptual influence is not asserted where this packet has only thematic similarity.
limitations: The packet is a historically grounded teaching synthesis, not a comprehensive historiography.
Formal expressivity does not establish practical learnability, biological realism, or general intelligence.
No source is represented as making claims about twenty-first-century foundation models.
